evidence.M1: R1-02: 'The spec row drops the re-read after the second timeout and bans CO-A3 even if a lookup would show the order cancelled ... CO-S15 hides the conflict: its Initial state makes every CO-A1 after the second CO-A2 unanswered' (round1-findings.md R1-02).
evidence.M2: R1-01: 'The spec's world in CO-S17 row 3 cannot exist: the order is cancelled, yet the tool reports it not cancelled ... The input adds the outcome without saying how to handle it' and the required 'the order is cancelled' contradicts the latest answer (round1-findings.md R1-01).
evidence.M7: R1-06: 'No scenario has a confirming turn that also carries a change ... CO-S03 Turn 2 is scripted "in place of a confirmation"', citing G-02 'Any change to a proposal term after confirmation voids that confirmation' (round1-findings.md R1-06).
evidence.M8: R1-18 (a): 'CO-02 is an "ask only when" rule ... No scenario has a customer who names no order while exactly one order is open ... An agent that always asks "which order?" therefore passes everything' (round1-findings.md R1-18); the no-open-order side is also in R2-12.
evidence.M9: R1-04: 'this prohibition appears only in the Scope "must not" list ... No rule in CO-01..CO-08 or G-01..G-04 states it. No rubric dimension in §5.2 checks it' (round1-findings.md R1-04).
evidence.M10: R3-02: 'The spec itself ends some trials with an order that is cancelled but whose refund is failed ... CO-S06 uses only an already-cancelled order whose refund is issued, so no scenario decides between CO-A4, a fresh CO-A3 (which CO-05 allows) and doing nothing' (round3-findings.md R3-02).
evidence.M13: R1-10: trigger 'the agent's first question that proposes cancelling HG-10482 and asks to go ahead' is not an event §5.1 defines; quotes checklist 'A User turn's trigger names an event §5.1 defines' (round1-findings.md R1-10).
